capacity:worker.title: Worker can't keep up
capacity:worker.message: At the diagram's own rates, it gets 10/s and handles 5/s (200%): its backlog only grows.
capacity:worker.rationale: Demand above what a service can handle never drains: latency and backlog grow until something times out. Live view's Show capacity has the same numbers.

secret-identity:vault\ninjected\tsecret.title: Worker reads secrets without an identity
secret-identity:vault\ninjected\tsecret.message:
Worker reads secrets from Vault
Injected label, but the diagram doesn't say what it signs in as. With a managed identity, it gets in with no stored credential to leak or rotate.
secret-identity:vault\ninjected\tsecret.rationale: A service needs a credential to open a vault, and one stored with the service is just one more secret. A workload identity (an Azure managed identity, an AWS IAM role, a Google Cloud service account) signs it in with nothing to store or rotate, and one per service gives each only the access it needs (least privilege).
